public_rationale: Zitron said the Fediverse report Newton shared 'isn't well-researched at all.' An independent fediverse specialist audited the same report. Part of the claim holds. The audit found weak and over-repeated sources, a main source with major factual errors that carried into the report, and missing relevant sources. But the same audit says the report gets quite a lot of information correct, is well structured, pulls in relevant examples and finds relevant obscure information. It also says the report hits most points a curious publisher needs. So the criticism of its sourcing holds, but 'not well-researched at all' goes further than the independent review supports.
limitations: I could not view the report itself. The verdict rests on one independent audit.
'Well-researched' is evaluative, and 'at all' may be meant as hyperbole.
